subject: Segmentation & KMS exportability — evidence and access mapping request
messages:
From: Natalie Park <natalie.park@datashield.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Segmentation + KMS exportability follow-up

Jonas, Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. HealthTech Labs is progressing through the privacy/security review and we have two outstanding asks from the PSQ that need a short write-up:

1) KMS exportability — we need a short statement about whether Redwood supports "customer-managed keys" with the ability for customers to export key material or whether keys are strictly non-exportable (HSM-backed). If there are deployment modes (hosted / dedicated / private) with different behaviours, please specify exactly which mode supports what.

2) PII segmentation & access mapping — the reviewers want a mapping that shows which internal roles (and subprocessors) can see raw PII versus tokenized/hashed outputs. Specifically they asked for a simple CSV or diagram they can attach to their compliance binder.

We attached our current PSQ answers and highlighted the two rows we need answered (psq_answers_v1.xlsx). Can you confirm whether you can deliver the KMS statement + a dataflow diagram showing role-based access and subprocessor responsibilities by EOD Friday 2026-09-08?

If a short call is easier, Edwina (cc'd) can join.

Best,
Natalie
DataShield Compliance — Third‑party Risk

Attachments: psq_answers_v1.xlsx (Excel workbook, 6 sheets)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie.park@datashield.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Segmentation + KMS exportability follow-up

Hi Natalie —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've looped in Marcus (infra/keys), Mina (privacy) and Irene (security evidence) to coordinate. Quick answers and next steps below: 

- KMS exportability: short answer up front — hosted Redwood API does NOT provide key export. Keys that protect our hosted tenant encryption are managed by our cloud provider and are non-exportable HSM keys. For Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments we support customer-managed KMS integrations (bring-your-own-key) where customers retain custody; key exportability depends on the customer's KMS configuration and HSM policies. Marcus will confirm the exact wording for an attestation document.

- PII segmentation / access mapping: we can provide a dataflow diagram (PNG) that shows where PII is present, which Redwood services/processors access plaintext, and role-level access (SRE, Platform, Support). Attached is an initial sketch I had Marcus produce; we'll refine to include subprocessors and explicit field-level mapping.

Can we aim to provide: 
  * KMS attestation draft (one page) by EOD Thursday 2026-09-04
  * Detailed dataflow + CSV mapping of PII fields -> roles/subprocessors by EOD Friday 2026-09-08

If you need the attestation sooner for procurement, let us know and we'll prioritise. Planning a 30m sync on Thursday morning if that helps.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Technical Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-04T08:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Segmentation + KMS exportability follow-up — technical detail

Hi Natalie, Jonas —

Following up with the technical detail for the attestation and the PII access mapping. Below is language we can include verbatim in the KMS attestation doc. I will produce a one‑page PDF (kms_attestation_stub.pdf) for signature if that meets your requirements.

KMS statement (draft):
- Hosted (Redwood API): encryption-at-rest and tenant isolation rely on cloud provider-managed KMS keys that are HSM-backed and non-exportable. Customers on hosted plans do not have the ability to export key material.
- Dedicated: Dedicated clusters can be configured to use customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. Key exportability is subject to the customer's KMS configuration and HSM policy; Redwood does not export key material on behalf of customers.
- Private (VPC / on‑prem): Customers may install and manage their own KMS/HSM; Redwood supports integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault, Thales/HSM appliances) but does not extract or retain key material.

Subprocessor involvement for encryption/key handling (short list):
- AWS (KMS/KMS‑integrations) — handles KMS operations in hosted/dedicated regions
- Google Cloud (Cloud KMS) — for GCP-hosted clusters
- Azure Key Vault — for Azure-hosted clusters
- HashiCorp (Vault) — used in Dedicated control-plane environments for secret rotation (no key export)

Note: access to plaintext PII is tightly controlled. Roles that may access decrypted data as part of debugging or on-call incident response are restricted to a small, audited set of SREs and Product Engineers and require Just‑In‑Time (JIT) approval via our ticketing + approval flow. Mina and Irene, please add any policy references we should point Natalie to (SRE access ⟶ internal policy doc).

I'll attach the attestation stub; it includes the above language plus a signature block.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer — Key Management
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is really helpful and close to what we need. Two quick asks to close the binder: 

1) Can you produce a single artefact (PDF) that contains: the KMS attestation language, the dataflow diagram with PII fields highlighted, and a short CSV appendix that maps each PII field to Redwood role(s) + subprocessors? That will allow our security reviewer to attach everything at once.

2) For the CSV appendix, please include an explicit column called "raw_access_allowed" with values TRUE/FALSE (so it's machine readable for their tooling).

If you can deliver the combined PDF + CSV by EOD Monday 2026-09-08 we'll be in a good place for completing vendor approval. I'm happy to take a 20m screen‑share if that helps finalize the field-level mapping. Edwina and I are available 09:00–11:00 CET on Monday.

I'll also attach the updated PSQ extract we want you to populate (security_questionnaire_redwood_fill.pdf) — we prefilled context so you don't need to start from scratch.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Natalie Park
DataShield Compliance
